ai_summary: Great Britain is currently generating 5.7 GW of wind power, with estimated Scottish wind output delivering 2.8 GW, operating at 27.7% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This abundant regional generation drives Scottish carbon intensity down to an impressive 4 gCO2/kWh, standing in stark contrast to the GB-wide carbon intensity of 177 gCO2/kWh. However, cross-border transmission limits prevent this clean electricity from flowing south where demand is highest. Consequently, 7,441 MWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a substantial constraint cost of about £232,865. To replace this lost renewable output, thermal generation elsewhere burned an estimated 1,413,695 m3 of gas, releasing an unnecessary 2,604 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere. Annualised from today’s pace, the total yearly cost of curtailment reaches approximately £85 million. Distributed across total national electricity demand, this adds an estimated £0.30/MWh to everybody’s invoice in the UK, which equates to roughly £31/MWh for each curtailed unit. Resolving grid bottlenecks remains critical to fully unlocking Scotland's low-carbon generation and protecting consumers from the compounding economic and environmental penalties of fossil-fuel redispatch.
